chapter: Breakup of Hines band to Lefty Bates
title: Billy Eckstine with the Hines band

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Speaking of Billy Eckstine, were you in the band when Billy came in?

Yeah, I was in the band when we picked him up. Yeah, he wasn't even playing trumpet then, yet. He learned the trumpet on the road while we were playing theaters He would practice in the dressing room on his horn.
Well, he's known for 'Jelly, Jelly,' and was it 'Water Boy,' was another one he made?
Uh-huh.
What kind of guy was he then? Must have been pretty young.
He was -- oh, yes, he was real young.
Was that his first --
I imagine the first big time, out of the Crystal Caverns in Washington.
How long was he with the band?
He was with the band until the band broke up.
In forty?
In forty. Then when the band was reorganized, he went back with the band.
Right. And that's when he made "Jelly, Jelly", wasn't it? And "Stormy Monday," or were you on those records?
Yeah -- huh?
Were you on those records?
I don't think I was on those records.
Maybe Chuck was on them.
Chuck was probably on them.
Was he doing blues when he first came with the band, or was he more a pop singer?
Well, he turned everything, blues and pop.
Did he have --
He was an all-around singer.
Did he have that pronounced vibrato then?
Yeah. Ballads and all that.
And he was pretty much as we know him now?
Yeah.
You know, the sound.
Yeah.
Well, were you in the band when Sarah Vaughan came in?
No, I left -- I'd already left the band.
And Dizzy and Charlie Parker?
Yeah.
That was afterwards?
That was afterwards.
